scalars.scalar_value: Minimum fifteen (15) years of progressively responsible research and strategy experience in health care, public affairs, journalism, conference production, strategy, policy, communications, thought leadership, market intelligence, research translation, or a related field.

items.item_text: Minimum fifteen (15) years of progressively responsible research and strategy experience in health care, public affairs, journalism, conference production, strategy, policy, communications, thought leadership, market intelligence, research translation, or a related field.

Exceptional writing, narrative development, and executive communications skills, with experience producing white papers, executive briefings, issue briefs, speeches, thought leadership, or other external-facing strategic content.
Experience convening senior internal and external stakeholders and building durable programs, forums, partnerships, fellowships, or other enterprise thought leadership platforms.

Establish and lead external sensing, insight, convening, and unique KP perspective development, building a durable capability that advances KPs mission, external influence, and leadership in the national dialogue on health care.

Identify and synthesize emerging societal, health care, policy, technology, consumer, employer, affordability, access, and market shifts; translate those signals into implications for KPs enterprise strategy, mission, reputation, and long-term value proposition.
Use a researchers toolkit that deeply analyzes historical and emerging trends in new ways and translates that research and insight into relevant impacts and perspectives for KP.

Develop KPs enterprise point of view on the future of health, value-based care, consumer trust, affordability, care delivery transformation, public purpose, and the evolving role of integrated, not-for-profit health care. Translate those unique perspectives into visible products for executives within KP, external stakeholders, and industry leaders.

Produce enterprise viewpoints, flagship reports, white papers, executive briefings, future scenarios, issue briefs, narrative platforms, and other thought leadership products, including original research and perspective development when needed, that enable KP leaders to communicate with clarity, discipline, and credibility.

Convene internal and external thought partners, including clinicians, researchers, policymakers, academics, employers, innovators, community leaders, market intelligence leaders, competitive intelligence partners, and health care stakeholders, through executive convenings, signature forums, fellowships, partnerships, and other organizational programs.

Serve as a connective enterprise capability linking market intelligence, competitive intelligence, policy, advocacy, research translation, clinical excellence, innovation, communications, community affairs, and enterprise strategy so KPs external narrative reflects evidence, mission, and business direction.

Partner across Enterprise Strategy and Business Development (ESBD), which includes Enterprise Strategy, Public Affairs, Business Development, M&A, and Strategic Partnerships, Transformation, and Risk to integrate subject matter, functional, and market expertise across the discipline into strategic research and perspective development.

This function will support ESBD leadership communications; market engagement including M&A, partnership, and strategic investment opportunities; stakeholder narratives, and executive visibility so ESBDs work is connected to the broader enterprise perspective and advances a consistent One KP voice.

House and strengthen institutional knowledge capabilities, including KPs archives, oral history collection, and related storytelling assets, in partnership with Internal Communications and other enterprise partners.

Evaluate and shape the appropriate role relevant organizational assets and programs, including signature convening spaces, speaker platforms, executive forums, international engagement, and potential partnerships that elevate KPs interests.

Deep understanding of the U.S. health care environment, including integrated delivery systems, value-based care, affordability, access, policy and regulatory dynamics, consumer and employer expectations, public trust, and the role of not-for-profit health care organizations.

Ability to work across complex matrixed organizations, influence without direct authority, and connect strategy, mission, policy, communications, market realities, and stakeholder engagement into a coherent enterprise narrative.
